next_step: Finalize SLA redline with procurement/legal; send revised term sheet by 2024-12-12; schedule exec sign-off call.
notes:
Account background: Axion Reserve Techworks (logistics / last-mile optimization). Large stateful chat + embedding workload for driver assistance + dynamic routing. Evaluating Redwood Dedicated with VPC/private control plane for PII and routing logic.

Recent timeline / activity (bullets):
- 2024-11-15 kickoff (ff-2024-11-15-axn-kickoff): intro AE/SE/Procurement. Customer: CPO (R. Singh) + infra lead (M. Osei). Covered scope: dedicated GPU pool, burst policy, compliance.
- 2024-11-20 architecture workshop: walked through VPC peering, KMS integration, audit log hooks. SE captured network requirements.
- 2024-11-29 SLA deep-dive (ff-2024-11-29-sla-review): Customer pushed back on 99.9% uptime; they require 99.95+ for production routing rules. Discussed credit schedule tiers and measurement windows (monthly).
- 2024-12-01 POC kickoff (POC-1987): 1-week perf run on medium-sized model (chat pipeline). Baseline metrics captured.
- 2024-12-04 perf debrief (ff-2024-12-04-performance-debrief): p95 latency ~110ms for short-context chat on reserved A100s (4x), p99 ~420ms. Throughput (steady-state) ~1.2M tokens/hour per 4-GPU pool for batched traffic.
- 2024-12-05 legal introduced redline to SLA (gmt-20241203-axn-legal).

POC / technical notes:
- Reserved GPU planning: customer prefers committed pool of 8x A100 equivalent (initial), ability to burst + autoscale to 12x for traffic spikes. Wants explicit commit + burst billing model.
- Throughput guarantees: Axion requests baseline throughput guarantee expressed as tokens/sec per-pool and a recovery SLA if sustained <80% capacity for >30m.
- Latency SLOs: target p95 <= 120ms (short chat 0-512 tokens), target p99 <= 500ms. Must specify measurement method (client-side vs service-side); they require end-to-end (client-observed) metrics.
- Uptime requirement: customer asks for 99.95% monthly uptime for dedicated pools. Redwood current standard 99.9% — negotiation point.
- Credit schedule ask: tiered credits with at least 10% service credit for monthly uptime 99.8-99.95, 25% for 99.5-99.8, 50% for <99.5. Customer wants credits applied to committed invoice and early right to terminate if <99.5 for two consecutive months.
- Maintenance windows: Axion requires predictable weekly maintenance window (1x/wk, 02:00-04:00 UTC preferred) with 48h advance notice for planned maintenance and strong guarantees around rolling restarts (no full-pool downtime). Emergency maintenance allowed but must be communicated and limited.
- Support response times (negotiated): P1 (complete outage impacting routing) - initial response 30m, follow-up hourly, target RM resolution SLA 4h; P2 (degraded perf) - initial response 2h, target 24h; P3 (non-critical) - 8h. Customer asking for named escalation path and monthly RCA for P1 events.
- Observability: per-route token/latency breakdown, request tracing, and retention 90d for traces and logs.
- Security/compliance: SSO (SAML), SOC2 & ISO27001 evidence, audit logs to customer SIEM via syslog, KMS-managed keys for model inputs stored longer than 30d.

Commercial / contract notes: 
- Committed term: 12 months minimum for the dedicated pool, pricing model: committed monthly + overage per-hour on burst capacity. Axion requesting reduction in unit price for commitment >$200k ARR.
- Billing: want credits applied against committed monthly invoice rather than future service. Legal insists on liability caps; Axion pushing for lower caps tied to uptime.

Quotes / customer voice snippets:
- "We cannot accept repeated 4xx/5xx windows during peak dispatching — routing decisions are revenue-critical." — R. Singh (CPO)
- "Credits are only meaningful if they offset committed spend; otherwise it's just a paper promise." — M. Osei (Infra Lead)

Open redlines / negotiation points:
- Uptime target: Redwood 99.9% vs Axion 99.95+ (primary blocker).
- Credit schedule & termination rights on repeated misses.
- Maintenance window guarantees (rolling restarts requirement).
- Measurement methodology for latency & uptime (client-observed vs server-side).
- On-prem validation runbook and acceptance criteria for private deployment.

Next steps (short):
- AE/SE to deliver revised SLA term sheet with adjusted credit tiers + rolling maintenance language (due 2024-12-12).
- Legal to prep limited early-termination clause for repeated <99.5% months.
- Schedule exec-level signoff call w/ CPO week of 2024-12-16.
- SE to run an extended 72h soak with increased tail traffic to validate p99 resiliency (tentative 2024-12-10 to 2024-12-13).

Internal notes / risk:
- Risk: if we concede 99.95 without stronger incident prevention we expose to heavy credit liability. Consider counter-offer: 99.95 for control-plane/non-RTR metrics; 99.9 for total end-to-end with exception for scheduled maintenance.
- Risk: customer may request on-prem-only controls after seeing billing; ensure deployment runbook and SOW have clear acceptance criteria.

Attachments / links: pricing deck (drive), SLA redline (attached to gmail thread gmt-20241129-axn-sla-redlines), POC logs attached to POC-1987.
